newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil insurance firms' premiums lower in 1st half.
newsitem.headline: Brazil insurance firms' premiums lower in 1st half.

text.p: Brazilian insurance firms' premiums in the first half totalled 7.3 billion reais ($7.16 billion), a drop of 1.4 percent from the same period in 1995, said Brazil's National Federation of Insurance Firms (Fenaseg).
The fall in premiums reflected an economic slowdown in the first half of the year, Fenaseg said in a statement.

Currently, the insurance sector accounts for 2.6 percent of Brazil's gross domestic product. But it is expected to grow to three percent of the country's GDP if the pace of economic growth increases, the group added.
Fenaseg also ranked Brazil's top insurance firms. It said Grupo Sul America leads the list with a market share of 16.62 percent and premiums totalling 1.18 billion reais ($1.15 billion).
Grupo Bradesco was the second largest insurer with premiums reaching 947,253 reais ($929,682) and a 13.32 percent market share, it said.
Grupo Itau and Grupo Porto Seguro were the third and fourth largest insurers with market shares of 7.23 percent and 5.98 percent, respectively, it said.
